title: build-v2 result
description: The one result of a build-v2 run, written to `<run_dir>/result.json` (E13 lane contract section 8, "the same result discipline"). Every run ends in one, including every stop. Two status fields, on purpose: `terminal_status` says which KIND of end this was, a `completion` (the run did its job and reports what it found) or a `stop` (the tool could not proceed); `status` is this core's named vocabulary inside that kind. Amendment A3 item 1 is why they are separate: a run whose named checks failed or could not run is a COMPLETION with a named result (`checks_not_passed`), not a stop, and the card simply does not move. Every response of the CLI carries `interface_version` and `plugin_version`; this document carries them too so a result read on its own says what wrote it.

interface_version.description: the version of this core's CLI interface

status.description: completed: the answer claimed complete, every named check passed, every out-of-scope path carried a reason, and the card moved to `built` (unless report-only). checks_not_passed: at least one named check is failing or was not run; reported with its output, card not moved; a COMPLETION, per amendment A3 item 1. not_complete: the answer claims `partial` or `stopped` and no named check failed; card not moved. answer_refused: the recorded answer is not recordable; neither acted on nor repaired; a STOP, because a run that may record nothing did not proceed. stopped: the tool could not proceed.

terminal_status.description: the kind of end. `stopped` and `answer_refused` are `stop`; every other status is a `completion`. Amendment A3 item 1's named completion covers failing checks and nothing else.

reason.description: one sentence naming what happened and what the caller can do

stop_reason.description: on a stop, what the tool could not do; null on a completion

stop_tag.description: a short tag for a stop, one of: `no_doc`, `no_slice`, `no_git`, `no_base`, `legacy_unplaced`, `card_drift`, `open_blocker`, `scope_unexplained`, `outside_edit`, `records_invalid`, `records_ambiguous`, `records_stale_source`, `records_conflict`, `records_failed`. An input that fails its schema and an unreadable answer file are not among them: neither ends a run, so neither reaches a result.

refusal_reason.description: on `answer_refused`, the seeded vocabulary's tag for why: `answer_invalid`

wrote_nothing.description: true when the run wrote nothing to the workspace and nothing to the log

source_set.description: the three lists and the base (lane contract section 8), computed from git; `docs/records/` is excluded from each (CR-3)

committed.description: changed since the base and committed, sorted

changed.description: different from HEAD in the working tree, staged or not, sorted

excluded.description: the prefixes left out of all three

sanctioned.description: paths of the source set the scope comparison passes over, each with the reason. Today: the ledger document this run is executing, which the loop writes into by design. A sanctioned path is IN the set — section 8 is the truth of what changed — and never in `out_of_scope`.

contract.description: what the slice says, transcribed from the build doc before any edit was recorded

path.description: the run artifact this was written to

named_paths.description: the slice's Footprint: the scope the source set is judged against

out_of_scope.description: every source-set path the slice does not name, each with the executor's stated reason. A path with no reason is a stop, never a silent pass.

reason.description: the recorded answer's `edits[].reason` for this path

named_in_not_in_slice.description: the slice states this path as a boundary

checks.description: one row per check the slice names, in document order, plus any check the answer reports that the slice does not name (marked `named_by_slice` false, so an unnamed check is visible and never gates the card)

source.description: where this row's result came from: the recorded answer, or this core running the command

rerun_refused.description: why a requested rerun did not happen, when it did not. A named check whose rerun was asked for and could not execute (shell syntax, an executable that is not there, a timeout, a report-only run) is `not_run`; the executor's claim stays in `recorded_result` and `recorded_output`

recorded_result.description: what the answer recorded, whenever the row's `result` is not the answer's own claim: this core reran the check and observed something else, a requested rerun could not execute, or the answer's command is not the command the slice names. Null otherwise: a disagreement is reported, never quietly overwritten.

recorded_command.description: the command the answer says it ran for this check, when it is not the command the slice names. Its output is that command's and is never reported as the named check's output

recorded_output.description: the output the answer recorded, kept apart from `output` whenever the row's `result` is not the answer's own claim

attribution_refused.description: why the answer's result is not this check's: the answer ran another command under the check's name. The row is then `not_run`

answer.description: what the executor concluded and whether this core accepted it as recordable. Never repaired.

refusals.description: each contents rule the answer broke, in one sentence

path.description: the run artifact the answer was stored at

card.description: the slice's card. It moves to `built` only when the answer claimed complete, every named check passed, and no path is out of scope without a reason.

reason.description: why it moved, or why it did not

document_line.description: the `Status:` line this run wrote, when it wrote one

records.description: everything this run asked the records component for and everything it wrote through it. Build raises nothing and clears nothing: the one event it ever writes is the card move it made.

log.description: the log's workspace-relative path, as the component reports it

levelled.description: CR-1: the document and its log levelled with `import-legacy` before the records were read

unparsed.description: `legacy_unparsed` events the pass produced; above zero is a stop (amendment A3 item 3)

native_rendered.description: how many lines of the document the component recognised as ones the log already records natively and imported nothing for (E13 amendment A4): the record lines `render` wrote, and a `Status:` line whose text equals the last card a native event holds for its slice. Null when the component does not publish the field, which is how one from before A4 reads; absent is not the same as zero and this core reports which it saw.

pinned_head.description: the head the run's state was read against, compared again before the append

open.description: what the slice has open, from `records.py state`

appended.description: the events this run appended; at most one, a `card_set`

recovered.description: the append had landed and only its record in the receipt was missing

wrote.description: did this run write anything to the log

refused.description: a refusal the component RETURNED. It is definitive, persisted in the receipt, and never retried.

identity.description: the six-field source identity as `records.py identity` computes it, with `docs/records/` excluded; the card event carries it

writes.description: every file this run wrote, in write order, each once. A run artifact under the run directory, the build doc's one `Status:` line, and the log through the component; nothing else is authorized.

resumed_half.description: on a settle, which half of the card transaction was missing

checks_changed_workspace.description: true when a check command this core reran changed the workspace (its six-field identity moved across the reruns). Such a run never says `wrote_nothing`: the bytes a child process changed are reported, and at report they are in the source set like any other change

unplaced.description: on a `legacy_unplaced` stop from the Appendix A stop check: every record line of the build doc that fits no Appendix A shape, with its document, its 1-based line, its bytes and why

receipt.description: the receipt path, when the transaction opened one

run_dir.description: the run directory every artifact of this run was written to, so a result read on its own says where its run lived and a checker can hold every run_artifact write to it
